title: Romeo and Juliet
description:
Your teacher will give the final grade after reviewing your work. Use GradeFlow scores and feedback as a guide to check your progress. The Essay Instructions (linked at the top right of your Google File) are the requirements for this assignment. The Grading Rubric at the bottom of that file explains how your final grade will be calculated by your teacher.


  1. ﻿Before you work on tasks, ensure you watch the Task resource videos.
  2. ﻿Review the Resource File (linked at the top right of your Google File) before you begin.

sections.title: Essay Setup
sections.description:
We'll cover the essay requirements, MLA formats, and GradeFlow basics in this section. Make sure you watch task videos for step-by-step instructions, learn to use the AI prompts and chatbots, review task hints, and understand when/how to use the "evaluate" button.


  1. ﻿Before you work on tasks, ensure you watch the Task resource videos.
  2. ﻿Review the Resource File (linked at the top right of your Google File) before you begin.

objectives.title: Essay Header
objectives.description:
Insert the heading in the top left corner of the first page. Do not skip any lines before the heading. Type the following information, each on its own line:

  • Your full name
  • Your teacher’s name
  • Class name
  • Date (Day Month Year – e.g., 13 May 2025)


The header must be Times New Roman, size 12 font. Keep text left-aligned. Do not bold, underline, or italicize.


  • You can use "Prompt#01: Understand Instructions In Context" from the resource file to help you understand this or any task instructions.
  • You can use "Prompt#02: Understand Feedback In Context" from the resource file to help you understand this or any task feedback.

objectives.title: Essay Title
objectives.description:
Before you work on tasks, ensure you watch the Task resource videos.


Below the heading, add a single blank line. Then enter the required title, Romeo and Juliet Consequences Essay. On the line directly below the title, input your subtitle. It must reflect the essay’s focus and connect to the actions, consequences, and analysis you explore. Center align the title and subtitle, and use Times New Roman, 12-point font.

You can use Prompt#01: Understand Instructions In Context from the resource file to help you understand this or any task instructions.

objectives.title: Essay Sections
objectives.description:
GradeFlow's evaluation engine will guide you as you write your essay, but to do this, you need to insert Section Breaks (Continuous) in specific locations. I strongly encourage you to watch the task video for specific step-by-step instructions. Failure to do this will result in a very poor score going forward.


You must insert FIVE Section Breaks (Continuous) in specific locations and follow specific instructions. Again, I strongly encourage you to watch the task video for specific step-by-step instructions.

  1. Section #1: Heading - Insert after the MLA Date Format.
  2. Section #2: Title - Insert after the Subtitle.
  3. Insert the section name in sections 3-6. This is a temporary placeholder text that you will replace later. This step just ensures you've set up your document correctly. EXAMPLE: Introduction Paragraph, Body Paragraph#1, Body Paragraph#2, and Conclusion Paragraph.
  4. Section #3: Introduction Paragraph - Insert after paragraph #1.
  5. Section #4: Body Paragraph#1 - Insert after paragraph #2.
  6. Section #5: Body Paragraph#2 - Insert after paragraph #3.
  7. Section #6: Conclusion Paragraph


You can use "Prompt#01: Understand Instructions In Context" from the resource file to help you understand this or any task instructions.

sections.title: Four Paragraph Essay
sections.description:
﻿Write the heart of your assignment.

Here you’ll draft and refine:

1. an introduction with a hook, summary, and thesis

2. two body paragraphs that each use quotes and analysis

3. a conclusion that restates your claim and leaves the reader thinking.

Automated checks will guide you on structure, word count, and evidence. Use the feedback after each attempt to strengthen your writing before moving on.

objectives.title: Introduction Paragraph
objectives.description:
Review the Essay Instructions for specific Introduction Paragraph requirements. Your teacher will give the final grade after reviewing your work. Use GradeFlow scores and feedback as a guide to check your progress.


Write an introduction paragraph that includes all of the following:

  • A well-written hook that introduces the topic of emotional decision-making or consequences.
  • The title of the play, the author, and a brief summary of the consequences you will write about.
  • A strong thesis statement.


Length: 3–4 sentences

Word count: 75–125 words


You can use Prompt#01: Understand Instructions In Context from the resource file to help you understand this or any task instructions.

objectives.title: Hook and Thesis Statement
objectives.description:
Use Prompt#03: Help with Thesis and Hook for help.


Craft a strong opening for your essay by writing a powerful hook and a clear thesis statement.

  1. Start with a Hook: This is your first sentence. It should grab your reader’s attention and use powerful or dramatic language to set the tone. Try to reflect the emotion, conflict, or seriousness of Romeo and Juliet.
  2. Title and author: Somewhere early in your introduction, mention the Title and Author.
  3. Strong Thesis Statement: Clearly state your main claim about the consequences of Romeo and Juliet’s actions. Be specific about which two groups were affected: their family, community, or future.

evaluations.failure_message:
Your hook appears too general and doesn’t reflect the emotional or thematic depth of Romeo and Juliet. Strong hooks in literary analysis often use powerful words to set the tone and connect to the key ideas of the play. These words show me that you understand the story’s emotional weight and lasting consequences.


To Improve:

  • Include a few more vivid, meaningful words reflecting Romeo and Juliet's major themes.
  • Focus your hook on emotion, conflict, and consequence to strengthen your thesis's connection.
  • Make the opening feel like it belongs to a story filled with passion, danger, and irreversible choices.

Revise your hook to better capture the seriousness of the play and grab your reader's attention right from the start.


Verify that the introduction paragraph is in section three. Rewatch the task video for additional assistance.


Use Prompt#03: Help with Thesis and Hook for help.

Your thesis statement is too vague or general. It needs to be more focused and take a clear position. A strong thesis should clearly state a claim and preview key reasons or consequences.


To improve:

  • Use words like "because," "consequences," "conflict," or "tragic" to show cause and effect.
  • Include an action verb like "argues," "demonstrates," or "reveals" to assert your position clearly.
  • Ensure your thesis answers the prompt directly and signals what the body paragraphs will explain.

Try revising your thesis to include stronger academic language and be more specific about what leads to the outcome in Romeo and Juliet.


Verify that the introduction paragraph is in section three. Rewatch the task video for additional assistance.


Use Prompt#03: Help with Thesis and Hook for help.

objectives.title: First Body Paragraph
objectives.description:
Write your first body paragraph following the structure below:

  • A topic sentence that clearly states which group (family, community, or future) was affected by Romeo and Juliet’s actions.
  • Two short quotes from the play that support your point (each under 100 characters and introduced with the speaker’s name).
  • Two sentences of explanation after each quote that connect the evidence to your claim.
  • A concluding sentence that restates how the evidence shows the impact of their actions.

Length: 8 sentences

Word count: 150–200 words


Use the Prompt#04: First/Second Body Paragraph for additional help.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph Evidence
objectives.description:
Review the Essay Instructions and make sure your Body Paragraphs #1 and #2 (Paragraphs 2 and 3) are in the correct sections of your document. GradeFlow will check both for required structure and how well you explain the evidence you've chosen.


Your goal in this task is to make your analysis stronger by using precise, thoughtful language to explain how your quotes support your point. Each body paragraph should do more than list quotes—it should show deep understanding of the play and connect those quotes to the larger ideas you’re writing about.


To succeed on this task:

  • Refer to specific events, characters, and conflicts from Romeo and Juliet—not just general ideas.
  • Avoid summary. Instead, explain why the quote matters and what it shows about the consequences of the characters’ actions.
  • Use language that shows insight into the themes, emotions, and outcomes of the play.
  • Choose verbs and vocabulary that clearly show how your evidence relates to the topic sentence.

evaluations.failure_message:
Your body paragraphs need stronger, more thoughtful, and vivid word choices to clearly explain how your evidence supports your point.

To improve:

  • Use words that show deeper thinking about the characters, their actions, and the consequences.
  • Focus on the why and how behind each quote, not just what happened.
  • Expand your vocabulary to reflect the themes and emotions in the play.
  • Check that Paragraphs 2 and 3 are in Sections 4 and 5. Rewatch the task video if needed.


The body paragraphs (Par#2 and #3) are in sections four and five. Rewatch the task video for additional assistance.


Use the Prompt#05: Body Paragraph Evidence Help for additional help.

Your body paragraphs need more precise language to clearly explain and connect your evidence to the topic sentences. Include specific references to the play and use relevant vocabulary to fully develop your ideas.


To improve:

  • Refer to the events, characters, conflicts, and consequences. Do not summarize.
  • Use clear verbs to show how they relate to the consequences you are discussing.
  • Use words that reflect the themes, emotions, and consequences in the play.
  • Make sure your explanations clearly show the impact of the characters’ choices and how they connect to the larger message.
  • Focus on using analytical and meaningful vocabulary that shows insight into the play's events, relationships, and outcomes.
  • Aim to use a wider variety of vocabulary that directly ties back to the novel’s themes and characters. This will make your writing more focused, analytical, and persuasive.


The body paragraphs (Par#2 and #3) are in sections four and five. Rewatch the task video for additional assistance.


Use the Prompt#05: Body Paragraph Evidence Help for additional help.

objectives.title: Conclusion Paragraph
objectives.description:
Wrap up your essay with a strong, thoughtful conclusion that reinforces your main argument and leaves the reader with a clear final impression.

In your conclusion, you should:

  • Restate your thesis in a fresh way, reminding the reader of your main claim.
  • Summarize your two key points (the consequences for the two groups you wrote about).
  • Reflect on the lasting message of Romeo and Juliet. What should we learn from the consequences of their actions?

sections.description: This section covers how to name a file so it is useful to the individual and/or system receiving it.

objectives.title: File Name
objectives.description:
When turning in assignments, it's important to name your Google Docs or other files clearly so your teacher can easily identify your work. Use the following naming convention every time you submit an assignment.


﻿Naming Convention: Last Name, First Name | Assignment Title | Class Period or Section


Example: If your name is Todd Benrud, you're turning in the Romeo and Juliet Consequences Essay, and you're in Period 5, then your file should be named: Benrud, Todd | Romeo and Juliet Consequences Essay | Period 5

sections.title: Teacher Review
sections.description:
These tasks will not be graded until you submit the assignment to your teacher. After you click the "Evaluate" button, you will see a "Turn In Assignment" button in the popup window. Click that to turn this into your teacher.


All following tasks will be graded by your teacher using the grading rubric at the bottom of the Assignment Instructions doc.

objectives.title: Intro Paragraph
objectives.description: Your introduction will be graded on four main parts: a strong hook that grabs attention, background information that includes the title and author, a clear summary of the text, and a thesis that directly answers the prompt. The strongest essays include all of these elements written clearly and effectively. Partial credit will be given if one or more parts are weak or missing. To earn full points, make sure your hook is compelling, your background is complete, your summary is clear, and your thesis directly responds to the prompt.

data.user_prompt:
`Grading Criteria`
First, review the entire essay to determine whether it is about Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare. Only proceed if the Pre-Check passes. If it fails, return a score of zero. 

1) The first paragraph is the Introduction Paragraph: Evaluate each submission by assessing three elements—hook, background, and thesis—against four performance bands (Exceeds = 5, Meets = 4, Developing = 3.5, Does Not Meet = 2.5). For the hook, check whether it is strong and engaging (Exceeds), merely present (Meets), weak or unclear (Developing), or missing/incorrect (Does Not Meet). For the background, verify that it names the work’s title and author and provides an accurate, concise summary (Exceeds), gives an adequate summary (Meets), lists title and author but offers a weak or missing summary (Developing), or fails two or more components (Does Not Meet). For the thesis, determine if it clearly and eloquently addresses the prompt (Exceeds), directly answers the prompt (Meets), is vague/off-prompt (Developing), or is missing/incorrect along with another element (Does Not Meet). Assign the highest band for which all criteria are met, then output a numeric score (5, 4, 3.5, 2.5), the corresponding descriptor, targeted feedback on each element, and a brief overall comment.
data.system_prompt:
You are an educational assessment and feedback specialist working in a project-based education platform. Your role is to pre-grade ‘student_submission’ for a classroom teacher using the ‘Scoring Rubric’ and ‘Grading Criteria’ listed below. All feedback must be appropriate in a school setting. Student feedback must be encouraging and support learning. 

1) Review the student-submitted files.
1.1) The student file is the included JSON file.

2) Evaluate the student-submitted files using the Grading Criteria and this scoring rubric.
2.1) 0 Points: No work or completely irrelevant; no evidence of understanding.
2.2) 1 Point: Minimal engagement; responses are incorrect or off-topic, showing inadequate understanding.
2.3) 2 Points: Partial understanding; incomplete or flawed responses.
2.4) 3 Points: Satisfactory understanding; generally correct with minor errors.
2.5) 4 Points: Proficient understanding; accurate and detailed with minor omissions.
2.6) 5 Points: Exemplary mastery; thorough, insightful, error-free, exceeding expectations.


3) Provide Formative Feedback to the Student:
3.1) For each criterion, provide specific, targeted feedback explaining why the student received their score. If the student lost points, include one concrete step they can take to improve. Keep feedback clear and constructive in two sentences.
3.2) Overall Feedback: Tailor overall feedback based on the total score
3.2.a) Score = 5: Congratulate them on their performance. Limit feedback to 1 sentence.
3.2.b) Score between 3–4: Provide specific improvement areas to reach full mastery. Limit feedback to 3 sentences.
3.2.c) Score between 0–2: Focus on specific, actionable guidance to help the student meet the basic requirements. Limit feedback to 2 sentences.

4) Provide a Critical Assessment to the Classroom Teacher:
4.1) For each criterion, clearly justify the assigned score by referencing specific gaps or errors.
4.2) Overall Assessment: Summarize criterion feedback and improvement areas so the teacher understands the student’s performance.

objectives.description: Your first body paragraph will be graded on how well you support your claim with evidence. To earn full credit, include two well-chosen quotes that clearly support your argument and introduce each quote smoothly. Partial credit is given if the quotes are present but weak, off-topic, or lack proper introductions. You’ll lose points if one or both quotes are missing or fail to support your claim.
